topics.title: Meaning and Types of Performance of Contract
explain: Performance of contract means fulfilling all obligations created under an agreement.
Section 37 mandates that parties must either perform or offer to perform their promises.
Performance is excused only when dispensed with or allowed under law.
Actual Performance occurs when both parties completely fulfill their respective duties.
Attempted Performance (Tender) happens when the promisor offers to perform but the promisee refuses.
topics.example: X borrows ₹5,00,000 from Y and repays it on the due date. This is actual performance.
remember: Actual performance completely satisfies contract duties for both parties.
Valid tender frees the promisor from liability for non-performance.
mistakes: Confusing tender of performance with breach of contract; tender is a valid offer to perform.

quiz.q: What happens when a promisor offers to perform on time, but the promisee refuses to accept it?
quiz.why: Attempted performance or tender occurs when performance is offered as agreed but rejected by the promisee.

quiz.q: Under Section 37, when can performance of a contract be excused?
o: Only when dispensed or excused under legal provisions
quiz.why: Section 37 states performance is mandatory unless dispensed with or excused by the Contract Act or any other law.

topics.title: Conditions for a Valid Tender or Attempted Performance
explain: A tender must be unconditional to be legally valid.
It must be made at a proper time and place during normal business hours.
The promisee must be given a reasonable opportunity to inspect the goods.
The tender must be made for the whole obligation, not partial performance.
topics.example: A offers to deliver 80 out of 100 contracted cotton bales. This is an invalid tender because it is partial.
remember: Offering partial payment or partial goods makes the tender invalid.
Tender must happen during normal business hours at the agreed place.
mistakes: Assuming an offer to perform late at night (e.g., 2 AM) without agreement is a valid tender.

quiz.q: A promises to pay principal plus interest, but offers to repay only the principal amount. Is this a valid tender?
o: No, because tender must be for the whole obligation
Yes, if debtor is facing hardship
quiz.why: A valid tender must be for the entire obligation; partial performance makes it invalid under Section 38.

quiz.q: Why must a buyer be given a reasonable opportunity to inspect goods upon tender?
o: To satisfy quality and quantity contracted
It is not required by law
quiz.why: Section 38 requires giving the promisee a reasonable chance to verify that goods match contract specifications.

topics.title: By Whom a Contract May Be Performed
explain: Contracts involving personal skill or confidence must be performed by the promisor personally.
Where personal skill is not required, the promisor or their representative may employ an agent.
Upon death of the promisor, legal representatives are bound unless personal skill was involved.
Legal representatives' liability is strictly limited to the value of inherited property.
Accepting performance from a third person discharges the promisor from liability.
topics.example: A promises to paint a picture for B. A must perform personally; his heir cannot paint it upon A's death.
remember: Legal heirs are liable only up to the extent of property inherited.
Accepting 3rd party performance completely releases the original promisor.
mistakes: Believing legal heirs must pay deceased debtor's liabilities from their personal pockets.

quiz.q: What happens if a creditor accepts ₹60,000 from a third party C towards A's debt of ₹1,00,000?
o: Creditor can still sue A for ₹1,00,000
Creditor can sue A only for the remaining ₹40,000
Third party C becomes liable for full amount
quiz.why: Under Section 41, accepting performance from a third person discharges the promisor to that extent.

quiz.q: If A dies leaving an estate of ₹12,000 but owes B ₹15,000, how much are A's legal representatives liable to pay?
quiz.why: Legal representatives' liability is limited strictly to the value of property inherited from the deceased.

topics.title: Distinction Between Succession and Assignment
explain: Succession occurs by process of law upon death or insolvency.
In succession, both rights (benefits) and liabilities (burdens) devolve on the legal heir.
Assignment takes place by voluntary act of the parties during their lifetime.
In assignment, only benefits can be assigned; liabilities cannot be assigned without creditor consent.
A debtor cannot escape liability by transferring their debt burden to a third person.
topics.example: A son inherits his father's estate along with unpaid debts. His debt liability is capped at the inherited estate value.
remember: Succession transfers benefits and liabilities (limited to estate value).
Assignment transfers benefits only, never liabilities unilaterally.
mistakes: Thinking a debtor can freely assign their loan repayment burden to someone else without creditor approval.

quiz.q: Which of the following can be assigned voluntarily by a creditor?
quiz.why: Under assignment, only contractual rights/benefits can be assigned, not liabilities.

quiz.q: How does succession differ from assignment?
o: Succession is voluntary while assignment is legal
Succession transfers both rights and liabilities by legal operation
quiz.why: Succession happens by operation of law transferring both benefits and burdens, whereas assignment is a voluntary transfer of benefits.

topics.title: Liabilities and Rights of Joint Promisors and Promisees
explain: Joint promisors must jointly fulfill the promise during their joint lives (Section 42).
The promisee may compel any single joint promisor to perform the whole promise (Section 43).
A performing joint promisor can claim equal contribution from co-promisors.
If any co-promisor defaults in contribution, remaining co-promisors share the loss equally.
Releasing one joint promisor does not release them from contribution liability to co-promisors (Section 44).
Joint promisees have only a joint right to claim performance (Section 45).
topics.example: A, B, and C jointly borrow ₹3,00,000. D can compel A alone to pay ₹3,00,000. A can then recover ₹1,00,000 each from B and C.
remember: Liability of joint promisors is joint AND several (Section 43).
Rights of joint promisees are JOINT only (Section 45).
mistakes: Assuming that releasing one joint promisor frees all other joint promisors from the debt.

quiz.q: If A, B, and C jointly promise to pay D ₹60,000 and C dies before payment, who must perform?
o: A, B and C's legal representatives jointly
D loses the right to collect
quiz.why: Section 42 states upon death of a joint promisor, surviving promisors and deceased's legal representative must perform jointly.

quiz.q: If D releases A from a joint debt owed by A, B, and C, what is the effect under Section 44?
o: B and C are also released
B and C remain liable for full amount, and A remains liable to B and C for contribution
quiz.why: Releasing one joint promisor does not discharge other promisors nor free the released promisor from contribution to co-promisors.

topics.title: Time and Place for Performance of Promise
explain: Where no time is specified, performance must be made within a reasonable time (Section 46).
Where time is specified, performance must occur during usual business hours on that day (Section 47).
If promisee must apply for performance, it is their duty to apply at a proper time and place (Section 48).
If no place is fixed, promisor must apply to promisee to appoint a reasonable place (Section 49).
Performance must be made in the manner and time prescribed or sanctioned by promisee (Section 50).
topics.example: A undertakes to deliver jute to B on a fixed day. A must ask B to appoint a reasonable place to receive it.
remember: Reasonable time depends on the facts and circumstances of each case.
Delivery offered after usual business hours can be validly refused.
mistakes: Assuming the promisor can deliver goods anywhere without asking the promisee when no place is specified.

quiz.q: What happens if a promisor offers delivery of goods at 9:00 PM when usual business hours end at 6:00 PM?
quiz.why: Under Section 47, performance must take place during usual business hours; delivery outside these hours can be refused.

quiz.q: Under Section 49, what is the duty of the promisor if no place is fixed for performance?
o: Apply to promisee to appoint a reasonable place
quiz.why: Section 49 obligates the promisor to request the promisee to appoint a reasonable place for performance.

topics.title: Performance of Reciprocal Promises
explain: Simultaneous reciprocal promises need not be performed unless the other party is ready and willing (Section 51).
Promises must be performed in the order fixed by contract or required by transaction nature (Section 52).
If one party prevents performance, the contract is voidable at option of the prevented party (Section 53).
In dependent promises, failing to perform the first promise disables claiming performance of the second (Section 54).
If time is essential, failure to perform on time makes contract voidable at promisee's option (Section 55).
Agreements to do impossible acts are void (Section 56).
In reciprocal promises with legal and illegal parts, legal parts are valid and illegal parts are void (Sections 57 & 58).
topics.example: A hires B's ship to convey cargo provided by A. If A fails to provide cargo, A cannot claim B's performance and must compensate B.
remember: Initial impossibility makes agreement void ab initio.
Supervening impossibility discharges contract after formation due to unexpected events.
mistakes: Believing that accepting late performance automatically preserves the right to claim damages without giving prior notice.

quiz.q: What is the status of a contract where time is of the essence and the promisor fails to perform on time?
o: Voidable at the option of the promisee
quiz.why: Section 55 provides that failure to perform on time when time is essential makes the contract voidable at promisee's option.

quiz.q: A promises to sell a house for ₹50 Lakhs and add ₹75 Lakhs if used as a gambling house. What is the legal status?
o: Sale for ₹50 Lakhs is valid; gambling promise is void
quiz.why: Under Section 57, the first set of legal reciprocal promises constitutes a valid contract, while the illegal second part is void.

topics.title: Appropriation of Payments
explain: If debtor indicates which debt to discharge, payment must be applied to that specific debt (Section 59).
If debtor does not intimate, creditor can apply payment at discretion to any lawful debt due (Section 60).
Creditor can appropriate payment towards a time-barred debt, but NOT towards a disputed debt.
If neither party appropriates, payment applies to debts in order of time, proportionately if equal (Section 61).
topics.example: Murari owes Girdhari ₹12,120 (2018) and ₹9,680 (2021). Murari pays ₹9,680 without notice. It applies to the matching ₹9,680 debt.
remember: Debtor has first right to specify payment allocation.
Time-barred debts can be cleared by creditor if debtor remains silent.
mistakes: Assuming a creditor can appropriate an unallocated payment to a disputed debt.

quiz.q: If a debtor owes multiple debts and pays money without specifying which debt to clear, what can the creditor do?
o: Can apply to any lawful debt due, including time-barred debt
Must apply to newest debt only
quiz.why: Section 60 allows creditor discretion to apply unappropriated funds to any valid debt, even if time-barred, but not disputed debts.

quiz.q: If neither debtor nor creditor appropriates a payment, how is it applied under Section 61?
o: In order of time (oldest debt first)
quiz.why: Section 61 specifies that payment shall be applied in discharge of debts in order of time.

topics.title: Contracts Which Need Not Be Performed
explain: Novation: Substituting a new contract for an old one discharges the original contract (Section 62).
Rescission: Cancelling a contract by mutual agreement ends obligations without creating a new contract.
Alteration: Changing contract terms by mutual consent rescinds original contract terms.
Remission/Waiver: Promisee may dispense with or accept lesser satisfaction of debt (Section 63).
Restoration of Benefit: Voidable contract rescinded requires restoring benefits received (Section 64).
Void Agreement/Contract: Any advantage received under void agreement must be restored (Section 65).
Refusal of Facilities: If promisee neglects to provide reasonable facilities, promisor is excused (Section 67).
topics.example: A owes B ₹5,00,000. B accepts ₹2,00,000 in full satisfaction. The entire ₹5,00,000 debt is discharged by remission.
remember: Novation can change terms or contracting parties; Alteration changes terms only.
Security deposit for performance is not a benefit required to be returned under Section 65 if forfeited properly.
mistakes: Confusing Novation (new contract created) with Rescission (contract cancelled, no new contract created).

quiz.q: How does Alteration differ from Novation?
o: In alteration, terms change but parties remain the same
Alteration creates a brand new contract
Novation does not discharge old contract
quiz.why: Novation can change parties or terms, while alteration changes terms by mutual consent between the same parties.

quiz.q: A pays B ₹1,00,000 to marry A's daughter C, but C dies before marriage. What is B's duty under Section 65?
quiz.why: Under Section 65, when a contract becomes void, any person who received advantage must restore it.

topics.title: Discharge of a Contract
explain: Discharge occurs when contractual rights and duties come to an end.
Discharge by Performance: Via actual performance or valid tender.
Discharge by Mutual Agreement: Via novation, rescission, alteration, or remission.
Discharge by Impossibility: Via initial impossibility or supervening events (destruction, law change, war).
Discharge by Lapse of Time: If not enforced within Limitation Act period (3 years for debt recovery).
Discharge by Operation of Law: Via death, insolvency, or merger of rights.
Discharge by Breach: Via actual breach on due date or anticipatory breach before due date.
topics.example: A leases land from B and later buys that same land. Inferior lease rights merge into superior ownership rights, discharging the lease.
remember: Limitation Act 1963 sets a 3-year limit to file suit for price/debt recovery.
Merger extinguishes inferior rights when superior rights are acquired.
mistakes: Believing that anticipatory breach automatically ends contract without promisee's election.

quiz.q: What is the limitation period under the Limitation Act 1963 for filing a suit to recover a debt?
quiz.why: If a creditor does not file a suit within three years, the debt becomes time-barred under the Limitation Act 1963.

quiz.q: When inferior lease rights merge into superior ownership rights of the same person, how is the lease contract discharged?
o: By Operation of Law (Merger of Rights)
quiz.why: Merger of rights occurs by operation of law when inferior and superior rights coincide in the same person.
